name: Autosomal Dominant Focal Non-Epidermolytic Palmoplantar Keratoderma with Plantar Blistering

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Focal Non-Epidermolytic Palmoplantar Keratoderma

criteria.description: Presence of focal hyperkeratotic plaques localized to the palms and soles
Recurrent plantar blistering associated with mechanical stress
Histopathological confirmation of non-epidermolytic hyperkeratosis without epidermal vacuolization
Autosomal dominant inheritance pattern with affected first-degree relatives
No evidence of systemic or syndromic features

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of focal palmoplantar hyperkeratosis with plantar blistering confirmed by histopathology demonstrating non-epidermolytic changes, plus compatible family history supports diagnosis.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may assist but causative gene mutations are not fully characterized.

Development of systemic symptoms or syndromic features
